cards.title: Screen router: registry + navigation stack replacing the shell's hand-lists
shared_surfaces: packages/game/src/screens/camp.ts and screens/parley.ts are also in camp-season card B's write set (subtitle odds). Land one first and rebase; this card touches only the s.<field> state reads there, not the subtitles

packages/game/src/screens/pause.ts, chrome.ts, listen.ts and game-shell.ts are also in this context's card B (bindings). Build A first: B then adds one 'controls' registry entry instead of another hand-list
Screen ids written to canvas.dataset.screen (ui/ui.ts:377) are read by the Playwright smoke tours (packages/game/scripts/smoke*.mjs). Every id stays unchanged
acceptance: case 1 (the bug): a training bout ends, so results() runs and the stack is [training-arena, results]. Then push('pause') and pop() -> restore target is 'results' and the fake host's results() is called. Today game-shell.ts:284-290 calls arena.pause(false) + arena.hud() because arena.games is undefined in training mode (arena-entry.ts:556), so the player lands on the HUD of a finished bout, and results never returns because arena-entry.ts:1077 sees phase === lastPhase
case 2: open('camp') -> push('pause') -> push('settings') -> push('audio-settings') -> back() x3 -> visits 'settings', then 'pause', then camp is restored (camp() called once at the end)

case 3: open('menu') -> push('saves') -> back() -> menu() is called. open('camp') -> push('pause') -> push('saves') -> back() -> pauseScreen() is called. This replaces the returnScreen === 'menu' check at saves.ts:84 and the writes at saves.ts:99 and saves.ts:113

case 4: liveScreens() is derived from specs flagged live and equals exactly {camp, visit, calendar, board, journal, trial, listen}, today's hand-list at game-shell.ts:200-202. overlayScreens() equals {pause, settings, audio-settings, saves}, today's list at game-shell.ts:266
case 5: restore('training') with remembered state {page: 1} calls training(1). Today redraw() (game-shell.ts:294-305) sends every unlisted id to camp()

case 6: per-screen state. state('board').page = 2, then push('pause') + pop() restores cards('board') with page 2. A nav-tab switch through campHeader resets it to 0 (today's s.cardPage = 0 at chrome.ts:124)
case 7: registering a duplicate id throws, and restore() on an unregistered id throws instead of falling back to camp silently
premise: packages/game/src/game-shell.ts:48-66 - GameShell carries per-screen UI state as shared mutable fields (selected, cardPage, cardSelected, castPage, visitPage, returnScreen, held, lane, parleyText, parleyApproach, audioPreview, typing, textDisplay, currentMoment). camp, journal, parley, listen, saves and pause each write them

packages/game/src/game-shell.ts:200-202 - the screens that redraw on a season revision are a hand-list of string ids
packages/game/src/game-shell.ts:266 - the overlay screens that must not re-pause are a second hand-list

packages/game/src/game-shell.ts:284-292 - resume() decides from arena state, not from where the player was: with an arena it shows results only if arena.games is set and not active, otherwise it returns to the HUD
packages/game/src/game-shell.ts:294-305 - redraw() is a third hand-list (cast, visit, calendar, board/journal, trial, listen) whose else branch is camp()
packages/game/src/screens/results.ts:104-112 - results offers 'Save / settings' -> s.pause(), and Escape also pauses
packages/game/src/arena-entry.ts:556 - restart() (training) sets games = undefined

packages/game/src/screens/saves.ts:84, :99, :113 - the back target of saves is inferred from returnScreen, which load() overwrites with 'arena'/'camp'

docs/concepts/D3-non-combat-presentation.md:115-118 - the D3 split left 'the season session, the arena, the shared state and the router' in game-shell.ts. D3 4.3 asks for more screens next (weeks 3-6, progression screens). Each one today costs edits to up to three hand-lists and new shell fields
cards.rollback: Two commits: (1) router.ts + router.test.ts added unused, (2) the shell and screens switched to it. git revert of (2) restores today's behaviour, and (1) is dead code that can stay or be reverted. Screen ids are unchanged, so no smoke fixture moves.
cards.runner_up: CanvasUI intent layer: pull one device-to-intent reducer (navigate/accept/back/pause/hold/slider) out of the 1,138-line ui.ts, where key() (ui/ui.ts:274-331) and pollPad() (ui/ui.ts:846-894) duplicate focus/back/busy rules with drifting semantics.
cards.body:
## Summary
Replace GameShell's three hand-lists of screen ids, its single returnScreen slot and its bag of per-screen fields with a pure screen registry and a navigation stack. The fix that proves the design: pausing from the results screen of a practice bout no longer strands the player on the HUD of a finished bout.

## Description
The D3 split moved each screen into its own module, but routing stayed hand-written in game-shell.ts. Which screens redraw on a season revision (:200-202), which count as overlays (:266) and how each screen restores (:294-305) are three separate string lists. Navigation history is one field (:53). Paging and draft state for board, journal, cast, visit, parley and listen live on the shell (:48-66). resume() picks its target from arena state, not from history (:284-292). When a training bout ends, results() runs, the player picks 'Save / settings' and then Resume: arena.games is undefined in training (arena-entry.ts:556), so the shell unpauses the finished bout and redraws the HUD, and results never fires again (arena-entry.ts:1077). router.ts gives every screen module a spec: {id, live?, overlay?, restore(host, state)} plus a typed state slice. The shell keeps the session and the arena and delegates open/push/back/restore to the router. The three lists become queries over the registry.

## Flow
- Add router.ts (pure, no Pixi) and router.test.ts with the seven cases, using a fake host that records calls.
- Each screen module exports its spec. Board/journal/cast/visit paging, the parley draft and the listen lane/held state move into state slices.
- GameShell.refresh(), pause(), resume() and redraw() read the registry and the stack. returnScreen is deleted, and saves/load push and pop instead.
- Screen ids are unchanged, so dataset.screen and the smoke tours are untouched.

## Expected impact
A new screen (D3 4.3: weeks 3-6, progression) is one spec instead of edits to three lists and a new shell field. Pause and resume return to where the player was, for any screen. One real stuck-state bug is closed.

## Evaluation
Claim: navigation becomes data, and resume restores the screen the player paused from.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (router.ts does not exist, and case 1's behaviour is today's bug at game-shell.ts:284-290)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - vitest router.test.ts, then npm run gate and npm run build:game. The coordinator re-runs the smoke:u3 tour (26 screens), which must show the same ids in the same order.
Result: better
Gate: architecture

cards.title: Rebindable controls: one binding table drives input, remap screen and all hints
shared_surfaces: packages/game/src/arena-entry.ts is in arena-render: only the one 'ESC / START  Pause' hint string (~:699) changes, to a bindings call
game-shell.ts, pause.ts, chrome.ts and listen.ts overlap card A. Build after A and register 'controls' as a router spec
lab-ui.ts hotkeys (R P G H T L V B, lab-ui.ts:172-196, :485) are read-only here: bindings.ts refuses them as reserved codes, and lab-ui.ts is not edited
acceptance: case 1 (no regression): with defaultBindings, ArenaInput gives the same InputFrame as today for KeyW/A/S/D, Space (roll), ShiftLeft/Right (sprint) and Digit1-5 (slot, capped by slotCount). All existing input.test.ts cases pass unchanged
case 2: rebind(defaults, 'roll', 'KeyF') -> ArenaInput built with it: keydown KeyF -> frame().roll === true. keydown Space -> frame().roll === false
case 3 (conflict swap): rebind(defaults, 'roll', 'KeyW') -> {ok: true, swapped: 'moveUp'}: moveUp now holds 'Space', roll holds 'KeyW', and no code is bound to two actions
case 4 (reserved): rebind(defaults, 'roll', 'Escape' | 'Tab' | 'Enter' | 'F8' | 'KeyR') -> {ok: false, reason} (KeyR's reason names the Combat Feel Lab), and the table is unchanged

case 5 (derived hints): hudHint(defaults, 'keyboard', 5) contains '1-5 spells' (today arena-hud.ts:260 and :441 hard-code '1-4 spells' even for the five-slot Fire/Air HUD). hudHint(rebind(defaults,'roll','KeyF').table, 'keyboard', 4) contains 'F roll'. hudHint(defaults, 'gamepad', 5) equals today's pad string at arena-hud.ts:440

case 6 (persistence): validateSettings({bindings: {roll: 'KeyF'}}).bindings.roll === 'KeyF'. A record whose bindings repeat a code, name an unknown action or use a non-string falls back to defaultBindings. A record with no bindings field (every save today) loads defaultBindings. version stays 1 (additive field, per-field fallback), so settings.test.ts:30 is untouched

case 7 (remap screen logic): controlsReducer: select('roll') -> {awaiting: 'roll'}. key('KeyF') -> table rebound, awaiting cleared. select('roll') then key('Escape') -> cancelled, table unchanged. reset() -> defaultBindings
case 8 (listen): with moveLeft rebound to 'ArrowLeft', the listen screen's cover-left handler moves the lane on ArrowLeft and ignores KeyA (today listen.ts:60-65 hard-codes KeyA/KeyD)
premise: packages/game/src/input.ts:45-51 - roll (Space) and the slot keys (Digit1-5) are hard-coded key codes
packages/game/src/input.ts:179-198 - movement (KeyW/A/S/D), roll (Space) and sprint (ShiftLeft/ShiftRight) are hard-coded in frame()
packages/game/src/screens/pause.ts:64-69 - the settings screen lists the controls as static strings ('W A S D  /  Left stick', ...), and nothing on it can change them

packages/game/src/hud/arena-hud.ts:260 and :441 - the in-bout keyboard hint says '1-4 spells' while school-hud.ts:32-33 gives Fire/Air five slots (D3 doc :152-154: 'The settings hint reads 1-5'). The hint copies have already drifted
packages/game/src/hud/arena-hud.ts:440, screens/pause.ts:165-166, screens/chrome.ts:45 - three more hand-written device hint strings
packages/game/src/screens/listen.ts:39, :52, :60-65 and game-shell.ts:149 - the listen minigame hard-codes Space/KeyA/KeyD/Digit1-3 and repeats them in its hint text
packages/game/src/settings/settings.ts:213-232, :256-274 - one versioned settings record with per-field fallback already exists, so a bindings field fits without a version bump
packages/game/src/lab-ui.ts:172-196 - Lab hotkeys share the same keydown stream, so a remap needs a reserved-code list

docs/concepts/D3-non-combat-presentation.md:40-41, :70-75 - D3 goal 4 'PC-native input and settings: mouse and wheel, keyboard and pad glyphs'. The landed slice (:136-150) added scale, window, tier and motion but no control mapping. Remapping is not in tiger/backlog.md or any spark idea
cards.rollback: Three commits: (1) bindings.ts + tests (pure, unused), (2) input.ts, listen.ts and the hint sites read the table with defaults equal to today's codes, (3) the controls screen plus the settings field. Reverting (3) removes the screen and keeps the derived hints, and reverting (2) restores the literals. A stored bindings field is ignored by the old validateSettings (it rebuilds the record field by field), so a downgrade is safe.
cards.runner_up: Save preview: show each slot's day, gold, renown and whether it holds a bout checkpoint before 'Load season' or 'Recover previous'. Both are blind one-click overwrites today (saves.ts:57-74) and would need a read-only save meta endpoint (server/api.ts:188-192).
cards.body:
## Summary
PC players get rebindable keyboard controls. One binding table drives ArenaInput, the listen minigame, a new Controls screen under Settings, and every control hint (HUD, settings, footers, the arena pause line). The hint copies can no longer drift.

## Description
Today the keyboard layout is written down in several places. input.ts hard-codes the codes (:45-51, :179-198). pause.ts lists them as prose (:64-69). arena-hud.ts has its own two hint strings (:260, :440-441). chrome.ts, pause.ts and listen.ts each have their own footer. These copies have already split: the HUD tells a Fire or Air player '1-4 spells' while Digit5 now reaches a fifth slot. A left-handed player, an ESDF player or someone on a laptop without comfortable Shift+Space cannot change anything. bindings.ts defines the actions (moveUp/Down/Left/Right, roll, sprint, slot1-5, listenHold, coverLeft/Right), their default codes (exactly today's), pad glyph labels, a reserved list (Escape, Tab, Enter, F8, brackets, the Lab hotkeys) and pure helpers: rebind with conflict swap, label(code) and hint builders. The Controls screen is a pure reducer (select, capture the next key, Escape cancels, reset) under a thin canvas view. The table persists as an additive field of the existing mage-settings record. Mouse buttons and pad layout stay fixed in v1, but their hints come from the same table. Simulation inputs are unchanged: InputFrame has the same shape and default codes give the same frames, so replay goldens and parity vectors cannot move.

## Flow
- Settings > 'Controls' lists each action with its current key. Choose one, press a key: it binds, swapping with the action that held that key, and a notice names the swap. Reserved keys are refused with the reason. 'Reset to defaults' restores the table.
- Back in a bout, the HUD hint, the pause line and the settings list show the new key immediately (they are computed from the table, and the HUD rebuilds on settings change like its edge rebuild).

## Expected impact
A standard PC option that is missing today. The hints are correct for every school, and every future control lands in one table.

## Evaluation
Claim: one table defines and explains every remappable control, and remapping changes the input and every hint.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (no bindings module, '1-4 spells' literal at arena-hud.ts:260/:441, KeyA/KeyD literal at listen.ts:60)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - vitest (bindings.test.ts, input.test.ts, settings.test.ts), then npm run gate and npm run build:game. Default-table frames are checked against today's codes in case 1.
Result: better
Gate: direction
